items.title: Lesson 3 Focus Question: What can you learn from the position-time graph of two cyclists on the same road?

answer.html: Where each cyclist is at every time, when they are at the same place (where their lines cross), which cyclist is ahead, how far apart they are, and (from the slope) how fast and in which direction each one moves.

check.html: Each item is a feature that can be read directly from the two lines.

items.title: Lesson 3, Figure 12, Identify: Position-time data for a lab cart are shown both in a table and in a graph. Identify one benefit the graph has over the table.

answer.html: A graph shows the whole pattern at a glance: a straight line shows constant velocity, its steepness shows the speed, and values between the measured points (and the crossing point of two objects) can be read off easily. A table only lists the individual measurements.

check.html: The table is better for exact values, the graph for seeing trends; each has a different benefit.

items.title: Lesson 3, Get It?: Two joggers' lines on a position-time graph intersect at (30 s, 90 m). Explain what the intersection means.

answer.html: At the intersection the two joggers have the same position at the same time, so they are at the same place together (90 m from the origin at 30 s), and one is passing the other. It does not necessarily mean they collide, since they may be in different lanes.

check.html: Before 30 s one jogger is ahead; after 30 s the other is ahead.

items.title: Lesson 3, Problem 13: Describe in words the motion of the two walkers whose position- time graph is shown. Gina's line goes from 60 m at 𝑡= 0 to 24 m at 12 s; Hal's line goes from 20 m at 𝑡= 0 to −16 m at 12 s (east is positive).

body.html: Both lines slope downward and are parallel: each loses 36 m in 12 s, a slope of −3.0 m/s. Gina starts at a positive position (east of the origin) and Hal starts closer to the origin, also at a positive position.
Negative slope means moving west; equal slopes mean equal velocities.

answer.html: Both walkers move west at the same constant speed of 3.0 m/s. Gina starts 60 m east of the origin, Hal starts 20 m east of it, and Hal crosses the origin at about 6.7 s while Gina is still east of it. answer.html: No. Both show constant velocity, but the diagram gives 1 m/s and the graph gives 4 m/s. (They would match only if the dots were 8 m apart, or if the time intervals were 0.5 s.)
